house-gop-218-jan-2027.base_rate:
The president's party has lost House seats in most midterms since WWII (about 18 of 20).
Losses were 40 or more seats in 2018 (-41), 2010 (-63) and 2006 (-30).
A Republican net loss of 3 or more would drop them below 218, and the current Republican count is already near 217-220.

facts.fact:
On 2026-10-09 Cook Political Report moved 18 House races toward Democrats.
One outlet says Cook's most likely outcome is a Democratic gain of 9 to 19 seats.
I could not open the page, so this comes from a search summary.

Cook's ratings page dated 2026-10-16 reportedly shows about 185 Solid D, 17 Likely D, 12 Lean D, 21 Toss Up, 13 Lean R, 16 Likely R and 171 Solid R.
The snippet was garbled, so these counts are approximate.

The House Press Gallery breakdown of 2026-03-18 showed 217 Republicans, 214 Democrats, 1 independent (Kevin Kiley, who caucuses with Republicans) and 3 vacancies.
Ballotpedia reported 217-214 with 4 vacancies on 2026-04-20.

Cook's open-seat tracker lists CA-14 (D, Swalwell resigned 4/14), TX-23 (R, Gonzales resigned 4/14), FL-20 (D, Cherfilus-McCormick resigned 4/21) and GA-13 (D, Scott died 4/22) as vacated.
As of 2026-09-01 Ballotpedia said CA-14, FL-20 and TX-23 were still unfilled.
Ballotpedia reported the FL-20 vacancy on 2026-04-22, the same month as the other vacancies.

uncertainties:
I could not open any page, so none of the facts is verified against the page text.
All come from search-result summaries, and the quotes arrays are empty for that reason.
The Clerk's current party breakdown for October 2026 was not found; the vacancy count and partisan split are unverified.
The November 3 results and any recounts are unknown.
Special elections for TX-23, FL-20, CA-14 and GA-13 may be held before or after January 3.
Mid-decade redistricting and court rulings on maps (Texas, California and others) could change seat outcomes.
